summary.headline: Deepak Fertilisers Q2 FY27: record EBITDA of Rs 750 crore (+62% YoY) and PAT of Rs 394 crore (+84% YoY) on 11% revenue growth.
summary.overview: Consolidated Q2 FY27 revenue rose 11% YoY to Rs 3,334 crore, while EBITDA rose 62% to Rs 750 crore and EBITDA margin expanded to 22.5% from 15.5%. H1 revenue grew 16% to Rs 6,590 crore, H1 EBITDA rose 63% to Rs 1,595 crore and H1 PAT rose 93% to Rs 884 crore. Management attributed the margin gain to long-term LNG sourcing, higher in-house ammonia integration, better product mix and downstream products. The Dahej nitric acid and Gopalpur TAN projects are about 98% complete and are expected to start operations in Q4 FY27.

segments.name: Mining chemicals
segments.commentary: Volumes moderated on monsoon disruption but better realisations drove healthy revenue growth. B2C share rose to about 16% of segment revenue from 14% a year ago.

segments.name: Industrial chemicals
segments.commentary: Nitric acid volumes rose 14% YoY, though pricing was soft on higher availability. IPA volume was 17 KT, up sequentially, with strong realisations from pharma-grade mix.

segments.name: Crop nutrition
segments.commentary: Challenging quarter for the industry with uneven rainfall and elevated channel inventory. Croptek and specialty fertilisers were about 28% of segment revenue; profitability improved sequentially on realisations and subsidy support. Excess inventory is entirely in this segment, built for Rabi season.

guidance_outlook: Dahej nitric acid and Gopalpur TAN projects expected to commence operations in Q4 FY27, within approved capex budget; ramp-up to about 75% utilisation within a couple of weeks of start, 85% soon after, and above 95% the year after.

Dahej adds about 300,000 tonnes of nitric acid capacity versus current sales of 240,000-250,000 tonnes per year; Gopalpur adds about 380,000 tonnes of TAN versus current sales of 550,000-560,000 tonnes (60-70% increase).
Chardham Chemicals (Nagpur, Wardha district) expected to contribute from H2 FY28 as part of mining solutions, incremental to existing segments.
Crop nutrition fertiliser margins expected to normalise to roughly 5-7% in Q3 and Q4 as subsidy support flows through.
Margin trajectory of recent quarters expected to continue with plus-minus variation; management declined to commit to 22% EBITDA margin but said a good range is sustainable.
No major growth capex beyond CCPL and maintenance capex visible for next year; next growth phase to be announced later. Demerger/IPO still under internal discussion, with no timeline given.
capex_capacity: Dahej nitric acid complex and Gopalpur TAN project both about 98% complete, with trial runs ongoing in phases (WNA, CNA at Dahej; WNA and TAN at Gopalpur).
Project cost to be 55-60% funded by term loans; combined project cost referenced as about Rs 4,600 crore, depreciated over 25 years for about Rs 180-200 crore per year depreciation.
Chardham Chemicals Nagpur facility being revamped; commercial production expected H2 FY28.
Gopalpur ramp-up expected at about 75% utilisation from start of commercial production.
demand_pricing: Management expects H2 pricing to firm versus monsoon period in TAN, with mining activity catching up after monsoon.
IPA prices supported by supply tightness; early recovery in nitric acid pricing noted, though Q2 nitric acid pricing was soft.
Government subsidy announcement last week cited as support for crop nutrition; Kharif demand hit by uneven rainfall and high channel inventory.
Export ban on ammonium nitrate removed in October 2026; export market development started in November.
Eastern India plus Singrauli region cited as 55% of national explosives and AN demand; Gopalpur customers are existing Taloja customers.
New domestic TAN capacity from a competitor entering the market; management expects initial turbulence to settle.

qa_highlights.question: How much were the ammonia and Equinor gas contract cost benefits, and is margin sustainable as crude and ammonia prices fall?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to quantify, calling the benefit not material. LNG benefits described as structural; ammonia price changes are passed through with a time lag. Q2 had no material inventory gains since materials are just-in-time.

qa_highlights.question: What is driving the crop nutrition inventory build and when will it unwind?
qa_highlights.answer: Entirely crop nutrition, built for Rabi season after a soft Kharif monsoon. Liquidation starts with Rabi season.

qa_highlights.question: What capex is planned for FY27 and beyond?
qa_highlights.answer: No major growth projects beyond CCPL, which is due for completion in the next few quarters. Only maintenance capex planned for next year; next growth phase to be announced later.

qa_highlights.question: Status of demerger or IPO?
qa_highlights.answer: Still in internal management discussion; no timeline or decision given.

qa_highlights.question: How did the market respond to new TAN competition and pricing in the seasonally weak quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said new entrants are welcome and the market is growing; initial turbulence expected to settle. Pricing is value-based through composite offerings.

qa_highlights.question: Is trading revenue in chemicals rising, and what is it?
qa_highlights.answer: Trading is over and above manufacturing sales, mainly ammonia trading. Majority of trading is in crop nutrition; no nitric acid or TAN trading.

qa_highlights.question: What volume growth comes from the new projects and when will they contribute?
qa_highlights.answer: Dahej adds about 300,000 tonnes nitric acid and Gopalpur about 380,000 tonnes TAN. Contribution begins in Q4 FY27, partial quarter, with full growth in FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Operating margin outlook: is 22% sustainable into FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Management would not give a number; said margins should stay in a good range with plus-minus variation, not exactly 22%.

risks_watch: Commissioning of Dahej and Gopalpur in Q4 FY27 has already slipped from Q3; trial runs still ongoing.
Crop nutrition headwinds: El Nino, raw material inflation, phos acid availability and high channel inventory.
Softer nitric acid pricing and new domestic TAN capacity could pressure realisations.
Corporate and employee costs up 40%+ YoY, partly for project support; watch cost trend.
Chardham Chemicals mining solutions contribution pushed to H2 FY28.
Demerger/IPO decision pending with no timeline.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on the quarter and the integration thesis, but evasive on specific numbers: declined to quantify LNG and ammonia benefits, margin guidance and project EBITDA contribution. Tone was cautious on crop nutrition headwinds and on the timing of the demerger/IPO.
key_quotes: Deepak Fertilisers have delivered our best ever EBITDA and PAT performances in Q2.
Even as we come to the end of our capex cycle, the peak cycle that was there, our net debt- toEBITDA stood at a comfortable 1.5x.
The heavy lifting is behind us.
Not exactly 22%, but in a good range, it should be sustainable in a range.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: EBITDA margin rose to 22.5% from 15.5% (Q2 FY26), driven by LNG sourcing and ammonia integration, but management declined to commit to 22% and crop nutrition margins are guided down to ~5-7% in Q3-Q4.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Dahej nitric acid (~300,000 t/yr) and Gopalpur TAN (~380,000 t/yr) are about 98% complete with trial runs ongoing, targeted for Q4 FY27 after slipping from Q2 FY27, so commissioning is guided but timing has already slipped once.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.when: Q4 FY27 onward, full effect FY28
rows.why: New capacity adds about 300k t nitric acid vs 240-250k t sales and 380k t TAN vs 550-560k t sales, with ramp to 75% then 85% and above 95% in FY28; no revenue growth figure guided.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Only CCPL and maintenance capex visible for next year; management said the next growth phase will be announced later, with no date given.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: No upgrade signalled; management declined to quantify margin or project EBITDA contribution and flagged crop nutrition headwinds.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Commissioning already slipped from Q2 to Q4 FY27 with trial runs ongoing, and crop nutrition margins are guided down to ~5-7% in Q3-Q4 from elevated levels.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Chardham Chemicals Nagpur mining-solutions revamp is expected to contribute from H2 FY28, though the brief gives no product-level launch detail.

rows.label: Nitric acid and TAN pricing recovery vs new domestic TAN entrant
rows.why: Q2 nitric acid pricing was soft despite 14% volume growth, management expects H2 TAN pricing to firm after monsoon, but a competitor's new TAN capacity is seeding the market.

rows.label: Export market development after AN export ban removal
rows.why: Export ban on ammonium nitrate removed in October 2026 and export development started in November, but no export volume or revenue figure was given.

rows.label: Crop nutrition channel inventory unwind
rows.why: Excess inventory sits entirely in crop nutrition, built for Rabi after a soft Kharif, and liquidation starts with the Rabi season.

tone.note: Management was confident on the quarter, LNG and integration thesis and new capacity, but evasive on LNG/ammonia benefit size, margin numbers and project EBITDA, and cautious on crop nutrition headwinds and demerger timing; analysts pushed on margin sustainability as crude and ammonia prices fall.
